summary: @servicetitan/restrict-imports preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes a 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` hook runs `setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...zip`, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it (via `execFileSync`) to run the sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` containing heavy string/number-array obfuscation (thousands of hex literals, shuffled dispatch tables, mangled identifiers) and is not human-inspectable. The package advertises itself as a webpack import-restriction plugin — a pure Node/TypeScript use case with no legitimate need for a second language runtime or a large opaque binary blob at install time. Routing execution of an obfuscated bundle through a separately downloaded Bun interpreter at `preinstall` bypasses Node-oriented review and gives the shipped payload arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
